name: Nullframe Ghost Rig Shoulder Harness
description:
Over-jacket tactical harness in matte-black recycled ballistic nylon with grey ghost-stitching along the load-bearing channels. Four modular holster mounts — two chest, two flank — accept standard-format mag housings or custom inserts. A dorsal channel runs spine-length to accommodate spinal rig externals and neural port cable management.

Fits over most mid-weight jackets without bunching. Strap geometry adjusts via ceramic slide buckles that hold under 200kg of lateral pull. Popular with operatives who need to look like they're carrying nothing.
functionality: Four modular holster mounts configurable for sidearms, data-drives, medkits, or custom rigs. Dorsal channel routes spinal rig cables cleanly without snagging. Ceramic buckles are non-metallic — scanner-minimal. Collapses flat under a jacket without visible print.
what_it_says: You're prepared for something, and you'd rather the room not know what.
story_hooks: A specific mount configuration — left chest, right flank empty — is a known signal in certain Circuit circles that the wearer is available for hire.
Nullframe's ceramic buckles are non-metallic, but a recent Corpsec memo flags the harness's Dyneema channels as identifiable by millimeter-wave scan.
Someone was found wearing one with all four mounts loaded but no weapons — just sealed data canisters, all encrypted.
